name: N-Queens Problem
description: Place N queens on an N×N chessboard so no two queens threaten each other (no two in same row, column, or diagonal). Classic backtracking problem.
aim: Find all valid arrangements of N non-attacking queens on an N×N board by placing queens row by row and backtracking when a conflict is detected.
howItWorks: Try placing a queen in each column of the current row
Check if placement is safe (no row, column, diagonal conflict)
If safe: place queen, recurse to next row
If next row succeeds: record solution
If no safe column: backtrack — remove queen, try next column
Continue until all rows filled (solution found) or all options exhausted

time.bestCase: Must explore all possibilities — no shortcut
time.averageCase: Pruning reduces constant factor but still factorial
time.worstCase: Explores all N! permutations in worst case

complexity.spaceDescription: Recursion depth N + queens array of size N

realWorld: Constraint satisfaction problems — placement with no-conflict rules
Exam scheduling — no conflicts in same room/time
whenToUse: When solution space is finite and must be searched exhaustively
Problems reducible to placing non-attacking elements
alternatives: Dancing Links (DLX) — Knuth's exact cover, faster in practice
Arc consistency — constraint propagation for CSPs
Genetic algorithms — for very large N where exact solution impractical
